title: Past Lives, First Love, And The One That Got Away

commenti.body:
Nice job on the conversation. You write well!

Some counters.

First, the craft complaint about Past Lives feels hollow to me. It hasn’t been a conversation I’ve seen. And the example given feels quite subjective. Especially in the context of culture and country. You can easily make the argument that the sense of place is important. That justifies the shots of NYC and making the two feel within it rather than just focusing on them through close up and medium close up.

Second, the analysis seems to overlook the main point of Past Lives. There’s a reason it doesn’t have a title like “First Love” and that’s because the movie isn’t really about love. It’s about coming to terms with the lives we could have lead. The people we could have been with. Etc. etc. The film is more like Robert Frost’s poem “The Road Not Taken” than it is a romance. 

The cultural aspect is part of that as well. There’s a version of Nora who grows up in Korea. There’s a version who stays in Canada. But the life she chose is in New York City, married to this Jewish guy. And she has to come to terms with what that means emotionally, culturally, etc, for herself, her family, any children she has. 

[Full thematic exploration](https://filmcolossus.com/past-lives-2023-explained)

> There’s a reason it doesn’t have a title like “First Love” and that’s because the movie isn’t really about love.

One of the things I appreciated about it was I never felt like "will they; won't they" was ever the focal point.  Sure, sometimes the "why they aren't" was focused on, but it was always tied into the deeper questions around identity, coming to terms with our lives, etc.

Thanks for reading and taking the time to reply. I liked your points (and it looks like this sub did too XD).

I guess I could have given the "Road Not Taken" idea or inyun a bone at some point of this write-up. That being said, I feel like it still ties into my references to fate and, to a lesser extent, identity. Also, the "what could have been" trope is already often prominent in this sub-genre, "First Love" being one of the works that shares in its exploration. Perhaps I didn't find its execution in "Past Lives" particularly exciting and didn't have it come to mind when I was doing this write-up--although I will admit it was Important in the grand scheme of the film.
Agree,  the films are not the same
